notes_for_editor:
- All four sources are secondary or community sources (LighthouseFriends; Historic Wabana, which carries Joe Dwyer's narrative and keeper captions and credits a January 1955 Submarine Miner article; the Newfoundland 3D Lighthouse Gallery) plus the Coast Guard List of Lights. No primary record was read. Newfoundland was not part of Canada before 1949, so the Canadian Department of Marine reports in the corpus do not cover this station; no Newfoundland archive was searched.
- The Historic Wabana page reproduces the 1955 Submarine Miner article as an image. Its text was not read, so nothing is quoted from it; the page's own narrative is cited instead.
- Conflicts left open in the story: the request for a lighthouse (LighthouseFriends, early 1930s; the gallery, 1939); the start of mining (1893 identification in LighthouseFriends; large-scale mining from 1895 in the gallery); the position (northeast end, LighthouseFriends; northern tip, gallery; Eastern Head, Dwyer); Bill Clarke's years (1978-2001 caption; 1983-2001 Dwyer); relocation distance (roughly 200 m, LighthouseFriends; nearly 200 m inland, gallery; a few hundred metres west, Historic Wabana).
- Keepers: names and years come from the Historic Wabana captions and Dwyer's narrative. Keepers whose service ended after about 1960 are given only as the captions print them, with no other personal detail. Fred O'Brien, Sr.'s years are decade bounds, not dates, and are marked approximate.
- Staffing: the record's staffed status rests on the Coast Guard 2010 list (per the record) and on LighthouseFriends and Historic Wabana, which say the station is still staffed (undated). The 2010 and 2019 lists named in the record (Senate of Canada, 'Seeing the Light'; the DFO page) were not read here.
- The Lighthouse Digest entry (search snippet only) says the lighthouse was rebuilt around 2004. It was not read.
- The 2010 vandalism is reported by LighthouseFriends, which cites a news story of 3 August 2010; the news story was not read.
- Access: the record says 'restricted'; that is kept. The story says the grounds are open and the tower closed, as LighthouseFriends reports.
- Wikipedia and Wikidata were not cited.
- Fact-check 2026-10-28 (story edits): the story now states the 1896 need noted by Historic Wabana, the gallery's northern-tip site, and the 2004 relocation disagreement (about 200 m or nearly 200 m inland in LighthouseFriends and the gallery; a few hundred metres west in Historic Wabana). The 172.9 ft focal height is also given in metres. Quotations from LighthouseFriends, the gallery and Historic Wabana are paraphrased; the Keeper's Cafe name is the only quoted wording.
